attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The Yang-Mills boundary OPE coefficients H,K and a uniform o(delta^2) for reflected Wilson hairpin products in the locked algebra are not yet known.
steps: Normalize by positive diagonals; collar closed-cone passage gives N>=0, but target positivity is q=Nhat oslash Bhat>=0, not positivity of N alone.
At delta=0, q0=J has one eigenvalue n and nullspace 1^perp. Let P project to 1^perp and u=n^{-1/2}1.
Use the Schur complement of the u-block: q_delta>=0 implies S_delta=PqP-Pqu(u*qu)^{-1}u*qP>=0 on 1^perp.
Expanding S_delta gives delta PHP+delta^2(PKP-n^{-1}PHu u^*HP)+o(delta^2); negativity on 1^perp or ker(PHP) gives a finite determinant falsifier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The linear algebra is valid, but the analytic input identifying B_delta,N_delta and proving the expansion without new boundary renormalization is missing.

assumptions: Regulated reflection positivity gives N_delta>=0 for each fixed collar.
The RG topology is valid for all finite reflected collar probes.
Diagonal trace continuity and positive-contact vanishing have already been proved.
The boundary Wilson OPE supplies Hermitian H,K and a uniform o(delta^2).
Diagonals stay positive so the Schur quotient is defined.
definitions: source object: finite reflected Wilson collar OS blocks N_delta with regulated positivity and boundary Gram factors B_delta.
target object: continuum same-theory OS matrix M on the locked gauge-invariant Wilson core.
controlled interface: normalized Schur preimage q_delta=Nhat_delta oslash Bhat_delta after additive contact elimination.
same-theory condition: no boundary counterterm, no observable enlargement, and the diagonal congruence is fixed by predeclared Wilson renormalization.

equations.label: finite Schur preimage
equations.latex: q_\delta=\widehat N_\delta\oslash\widehat B_\delta,\quad M_\delta=D_\delta q_\delta D_\delta^*
equations.valid_when: Additive boundary contacts vanish and B_delta is the multiplicative boundary Gram factor for the same locked Wilson block.

equations.label: rank-one collar expansion
equations.valid_when: The reflected Wilson boundary OPE has a C^2 collar expansion uniform for the finite block.

equations.label: second-order tangent gates
equations.valid_when: Necessary for q_delta>=0 for all small delta; a negative value is a valid finite Wilson falsifier.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find locked Wilson hairpins whose computed H,K violate the first or second gate; then collar positivity does not imply target OS positivity for the same theory.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns boundary OPE coefficients into a concrete OS tangent-cone test linking formal closed-cone positivity to Wilson hairpin estimates.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If a same-theory Wilson collar quotient q_delta=J+delta H+delta^2K+o(delta^2) is OS-positive for all small collars, then PHP>=0 and the Schur-corrected second form is nonnegative on ker(PHP); either violation is a finite falsifier.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if RG topology cannot control reflected Wilson collar quotients or if boundary renormalization changes the locked algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if H,K are computed or bounded on a dense Wilson core and both tangent gates are nonnegative uniformly.
control_decision.reason: The branch produced a sharper finite obstruction with explicit computable coefficients, so learning remains high.

dependency_updates.description: The collar closed-cone step remains valid; the bridge now needs Wilson quotient tangent-cone estimates through second order.
The locked Wilson core must support finite hairpin blocks rich enough to test PHP and the Schur-corrected null form.
Topology must control normalized reflected Wilson quotients and their boundary OPE remainders, not only unnormalized finite forms.

falsifiers: First-order falsifier: a zero-sum vector x with x^*PHPx<0 in a realized Wilson block.
Second-order falsifier: x in ker(PHP) with x^*(PKP-n^{-1}PHu u^*HP)x<0.
Expansion falsifier: the boundary OPE contains delta^2 log(delta) or a nonuniform remainder, so the tangent lemma is not valid.
Same-theory falsifier: diagonal/contact renormalization changes the Wilson core, so q_delta no longer represents the intended OS matrix.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 219 upgrades the OS quotient obstruction from first-order PHP to the correct second-order tangent cone. The rank-one OS direction is not passive; eliminating it subtracts n^{-1}PHu u^*HP. The next valid falsifier is a boundary OPE computation of H,K for a finite Wilson block.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute H and K for a minimal three-hairpin reflected Wilson block sharing one boundary footprint; test PHP and the Schur-corrected form on ker(PHP).

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
next_cycle_queue: Compute H and K for a minimal three-hairpin reflected Wilson block sharing one boundary footprint; test PHP and the Schur-corrected form on ker(PHP).
